text: The dark-matter paper T14 fixes how much matter each of five dark towers holds, not what that matter is. This note builds it with the Standard-Model paper's construction. A constituent is an element of the spin-irreducible even ideal of the tower's conformal algebra, and its scalars are the commutant of the spin action there. We prove that this field is the division algebra of the next residue: the reals in the three-dimensional towers, the complex numbers in this tower and the mirror, the quaternions in the five-dimensional towers. One identity of the reversion pairing then says where mass begins (two constituents in three and four dimensions, one in five); the momentum-preserving mixings are the field's unitary groups; and, under the series' identification premise and one transposition rule, the gauge algebras follow. The mirror carries the Standard Model again. Both three-dimensional towers carry the abelian $\so(2) \oplus \so(2)$: two copies of single-flavour electrodynamics in $2+1$ dimensions. Both five-dimensional towers carry $\uu(3)$, dark colour and one abelian charge, with vector-like quarks, leptons and a neutral singlet; with an external imaginary unit both would carry the Standard-Model algebra instead. The towers of each odd dimension differ only in discrete structure. Three consequences follow. Neither the unit-ball rule's premise E nor T14's particle model has a mechanism in any odd tower. A cold mirror is an unstated exception to T14's indifference premise. No configuration of the towers as built passes the cluster, radiation and mirror bounds together. The algebraic results are verified in exact arithmetic.

title: What we assume
E: equal mass per unit ball
text:
\emph{Premise (E), equal mass per unit ball.} There is one length $d$, common to all populated towers, such that every populated tower holds the same mass $\mu$ per ball of radius $d$ of its own space. With $\rho_{r}$ the mass per unit volume of the $D_{r}$-dimensional space of the tower of residue $r$, at its representative under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}, and $V_{D}$ the volume of the unit ball $\B^{D}$,
\[
\rho_{r}\,V_{D_{r}}\,d^{D_{r}} \;=\; \mu \qquad \text{for every populated } r .
\]
The unit ball of the unit-ball rule is the ball of radius $d$.

\emph{What it replaces.} Premises R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}, equal mass per quantum) and R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}, one quantum per unit ball), taken in the length $d$, give E with $\mu$ the mass of a quantum, and E gives neither: it says nothing about what a tower's quanta weigh or how many there are (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}(i)). R1 and R2 are one model of E, the particle model. By the decision of 19 November 2026, E and not R1 and R2 is the premise of the dark-to-baryon total (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}), with the thickness of Premise R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) read in the same length $d$. R1 and R2 remain premises of the stored results that use a quantum's mass or number by itself.

\emph{What it does not fix.} E does not fix $d$ independently of the towers' densities, which are not observed, and the total does not depend on it: once E and R3 hold, $d$ is $\rho_{1}V_{2}/(\rho_{6}V_{3})$, the density of a three-dimensional tower against ours (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}(iii)). In particular $d$ is not tied to the spacing of this world's baryons. That tie belongs to the particle model, R1 and R2 together: E at $d$ with R2 in another common length is consistent, the quanta then having unequal masses. The stored results that give the counted thickness a value, today's baryon spacing of about a metre or its value at the deposit, rest on R1 and R2 for that. The democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is E with $d$ the de Sitter radius, given the stored reading of the sphere form, and the particle model is E with $d$ the common cell radius (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}(i), (ii)). E can hold in one length only (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}(iv)). It presupposes that the towers it names are populated, which for the four odd towers is Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}. Whether one length serves at more than one epoch is settled as for R2 (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-ball-clauses-hold-at-one-epoch-unless-hidden-direction-co-expands}(v)): only if the five-dimensional towers' hidden direction co-expands with ours, and otherwise E is a statement about the deposit.

\emph{How much it says.} For the mirror, whose space has the dimension of ours, E is equal density, which the population count gives separately on the proton-only branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}; on the burning branch the count gives $0.9948$ and E fails for the mirror by about one part in two hundred, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}(iii)). E with R3 holds for some $d$ exactly when the closed form's shares hold tower by tower and the two thicknesses are equal (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}(iii)). So E is the fitted relation stated as one law: it adds no support to the fit that is independent of the fitted number, and the series supplies no mechanism for it.

\emph{Refutation condition.} Observation can refute E with R3 only through the closed form: by a dark-to-baryon ratio that excludes $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi$, or by a composition of the dark matter other than the shares $V_{3}/V_{D}$. E with R3 says more than the total does, that the shares hold tower by tower and that the two thicknesses are equal (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}(iii)), and that further content is not observed.

title: P3: nearest-dimension representatives
text: Each tower is represented at the dimension nearest four; where two are equally near (the odd residues, three and five), the lower one with a single time, else the higher. \emph{Support:} P1's one metric read as minimality. Structural premise; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii) records the other windows. \emph{Note.} Premise (W) of \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-complement-window-lowest-causal}, that every tower's spacetime is, up to sign, a nondegenerate subspace of the frozen point's complement, is recorded as a costed alternative that restates this premise's window (with the single-clock filter it would replace this premise and the residue-$4$ half of the costed single-ideal clause of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(vi) by one hypothesis; at residue $0$ it admits the causal $(1,1)$ where this premise has $(2,2)$); it was found with the fit known and is not adopted. This premise is unchanged. \emph{Note (by residue).} At the odd residues this premise takes the lowest causal member, $(2,1)$, $(1,2)$ at residues $1$, $7$ and $(4,1)$, $(1,4)$ at residues $3$, $5$. At residues $1$ and $7$ that choice follows from Premise U (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}): the constituent field is $\R$ in every causal member and the stored pair count exceeds the real Witt index $2$ above dimension three, so U admits only $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$. At residues $3$ and $5$ it is independent of the descent: a model with those towers at $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$ satisfies every premise of the window-sensitive results other than this one, Premise U included, so there the window is an input (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.bott-shifted-model-leaves-the-odd-towers-dimension-free}(ii), (iii)).

title: R1: equal mass per quantum
text: The quanta of every populated tower carry the same mass $m$.

title: R2: one quantum per unit ball
text: A populated tower whose space has $D$ dimensions (under P3, \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}, $2$, $3$ or $4$) holds one quantum per unit ball $\B^{D}$ of that space, in one unit of length common to all towers: every tower has the same Wigner-Seitz radius. The rule presupposes that all six towers are populated, which for the odd four is the inference of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}.

title: R3: one cell per unshared direction
text:
In the sourcing rule, a tower's matter counts through exactly one unit of length of each direction its neighbour lacks, on one side: a five-dimensional tower's matter through one unit of its extra direction, and a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one unit apart along the direction it lacks. the section ``The thickness: a contact mechanism'' gives a mechanism that returns this value and costs it.

\emph{The unit.} The unit is the length $d$ of Premise E (\claimref{dark-matter.e-equal-mass-per-unit-ball}): one length common to all towers, the radius of the ball in which E counts mass, and independent of how a tower's mass is divided into quanta. This is the fixed-common-length reading, adopted by the decision of 19 November 2026; it replaces the reading of 10 November 2026, in which the unit was each tower's own cell radius, the Wigner-Seitz radius of its own filling. Under R1 and R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}, \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}), E holds in R2's common length, which is then $d$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}(iv)), every tower's cell radius is $d$ and the two readings coincide; under R2 alone they coincide only if R2 is taken in the length $d$. They differ when R2 fails: with a tower's own cell radius $a_{r}$ as the unit the shares are $(m_{r}/m_{6})(V_{3}/V_{D_{r}})(a_{6}/a_{r})^{3}$, which Premise E does not fix, and with the common length they are $V_{3}/V_{D_{r}}$ under E alone (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}(i)). The title keeps the word cell: the cell is the unit ball of Premise E. The premise takes its unit from E, so where E is not assumed the unit has to be supplied in another way: by R1 with R2, whose common cell radius is then E's length, or by the democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}), whose length is the de Sitter radius.

title: Premise H1: a constituent's momentum
text:
A constituent has a spinor part $\psi$ in the tower's spinor ideal $S$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-tower-matter.ideals-fields-momentum}), carried by a map $T \to S$ that intertwines the action of the tower's spin group, so that the field of $T$ acts on $S$ through it; its momentum is the vector part of $\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}$. In dimension four this is T12's Fact 2.1 in the even algebra; in dimensions three and five it is a premise.

\emph{Note (what of H1 is forced).} In the causal towers of dimension three to five the quadratic vectors of one constituent's spinor part that are covariant under the connected spin group form one real line, spanned by this momentum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.constituent-momentum-is-the-unique-spin-covariant-quadratic-vector-on-the-spinor-ideal}). So, given a spinor part and a momentum that is quadratic and covariant, the formula is forced up to a real factor. H1 is weakened by that result, not retired: what stays premised in dimensions three and five is that a constituent has a spinor part in $S$ carried by an intertwining map, that its momentum is a quadratic covariant vector of it, the normalisation, and the additivity of momenta over constituents, which covariance does not force.

title: Premise H2: gauge algebras as hierarchy automorphisms
text: The gauge algebra of a tower's matter is the automorphism algebra of its minimal massive hierarchy, constituent slots tensor pair slots, as T12's Theorem 4.1 identifies it in dimension four, at observation level \cite[Thm.~4.1, Prop.~4.3]{ButlerT12}.

title: Hypothesis (S) carried to every tower
text: The constituent slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs, so that the composite's state space is the exterior algebra of slot and pair modes \cite[Sec.~5]{ButlerT12}. Used only where stated.

title: Premise U: the transposition rule (a definition)
text:
(U1) A constituent is an element of the spin-irreducible even ideal of the conformal algebra, as T12 defines this tower's, and its field is the commutant of the spin action on it. (U2) The hierarchy's first factor counts constituents at mass onset, and its slot group is the momentum-preserving group of that many constituents; the pair group is the group of mixings of the ladder pairs that preserves their canonical relations and the field's positive norm, the unitary group over the pairs' scalars ($\R$, or $\C$ where a complex unit builds the pairs), as T12 takes $U(m) \times U(k)$ \cite[Thm.~4.1]{ButlerT12}. The norm clause is part of the definition: no positive form on the pair space is derived, and without it the group preserving the canonical relations is $GL(2,\R)$; the compactness of every gauge group stated under U rests on it. (U3) Every complex unit used to build a ladder pair is an element of the constituent's field that the real algebra supplies; no external imaginary unit is adjoined.

\emph{Type: a definition.} The three clauses define what the series calls a constituent in another tower, its field, the slot and pair groups, and which complex units are admitted; they assert nothing about nature that could be derived or refuted, and can only be replaced by another definition (Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.branches-break-u-what-they-give} lists what other choices give). The definition has consequences through what it excludes: with it, the lowest-causal choice of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} at residues $1$ and $7$ follows. Results stated under Premise U hold for the objects so defined; the entity keeps the status of a premise so that those results show the choice among their conditions.

title: Introduction
Setting, imports and premises
text:
Throughout, a tower is $V = \R^{p,q}$ with an orthonormal basis $\{e_{a}\}$, $Q(e_{a}) = e_{a}^{2} = \pm 1$, and $\Cl(V) = \Cl(p,q)$ its Clifford algebra, with even subalgebra $\Cl^{0}(V)$, reversion $x \mapsto \rev{x}$, grade involution $x \mapsto \hat{x}$ and grade projection $\ip{\cdot}_{k}$. In a causal signature ($\min(p,q) = 1$) the \emph{time direction} $e_{t}$ is the one basis vector of the minority sign, as in T14's convention \cite[Prop.~3.1]{ButlerT14}, and $Q(e_{t}) = \pm 1$ accordingly. The tower's conformal algebra is $\Cl(\hatV)$ with $\hatV = V \oplus \R^{1,1}$, that is $\Cl(p+1, q+1)$. The pseudoscalar of an algebra of dimension $n$ is $\omega = e_{1}e_{2}\cdots e_{n}$, central when $n$ is odd, with $Q(\omega) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$.

The objects that the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} and T12 describe in twistor language are, here, the even ideals of the conformal algebra and their elements; this note uses only the latter.

title: Imported: the structure of real Clifford algebras
text: (i) For $q \geq 1$, $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$, by $e_{a} \mapsto e_{a}e_{n}$ with $Q(e_{n}) = -1$; for $p \geq 1$, $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(q, p-1)$. (ii) $\Cl(p,q)$ is a matrix algebra over $D \in \{\R, \C, \HH\}$, or a sum of two, with $D$ fixed by $p - q \bmod 8$: $\R$ at $0, 1, 2$; $\C$ at $3, 7$; $\HH$ at $4, 5, 6$. (iii) A minimal left ideal $Af$ of a simple or semisimple algebra $A$, $f$ a primitive idempotent, has commutant $\mathrm{End}_{A}(Af) \cong (fAf)^{\mathrm{op}}$, a division algebra (Schur), acting by right multiplication. Sources: \cite{Chevalley1954, Lounesto2001, LawsonMichelsohn1989}.

title: Imported: the unit-ball shares
text: T14's unit-ball rule rests on two premises: E, one length $d$ common to every populated tower at which each holds the same mass per ball of radius $d$ of its own space, and R3, a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one $d$ apart and a five-dimensional tower's matter counted through one $d$ of its extra direction. Under E and R3 the shares are $1$, $2 \times 4/3$, $2 \times 8/(3\pi)$, with total $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi)$ \cite[Prem.~7.2, Prem.~7.4, Prop.~7.6(i)]{ButlerT14}. T14's particle model, R1 (every quantum of every populated tower has the same mass) and R2 (one quantum per unit ball of each tower's own space, so a common Wigner-Seitz radius $d$), implies E and is not used by the rule \cite[Prem.~7.3, Prop.~7.6(ii)]{ButlerT14}; in it $d$ is this world's baryon spacing, $d_{b} \approx 0.98$ m, and the mass the nucleon's \cite[Rem.~7.9, Cor.~7.26]{ButlerT14}. E alone fixes neither. As fractions of the dark matter: mirror $18.6$ percent, each three-dimensional tower $24.9$, each five-dimensional tower $15.8$.

As fractions of the dark matter: mirror $18.6$ percent, each three-dimensional tower $24.9$, each five-dimensional tower $15.8$.

title: Imported: the cluster merger simulations
text: In the idealised Bullet-like merger runs of T14b \cite[Obs.~7.1, Table~3]{ButlerT14b}: (i) with only the mirror colliding ($18.6$ percent of the dark matter, as gas) the subcluster keeps a separate lensing peak on its galaxies and a mass-to-light change of $0.82$ against the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$; (ii) with the mirror gas and one three-dimensional tower's share of colliding fluid ($43.5$ percent colliding) the subcluster dissolves, and with more it dissolves too; (iii) with the mirror collisionless and $24.9$ or $31.6$ percent of colliding fluid, the subcluster keeps a weaker peak but only $0.55$ or $0.44$ of its central mass: the colliding fluid alone costs about half of it. In (i) the subcluster's own mass is $0.57$ of the cold-dark-matter run's, but mass and light leave together and the mass-to-light change, the quantity the observational bound is inferred from, is consistent. No run lies between $18.6$ and $24.9$ percent colliding. The colliding components there are fluids.

title: Setting, imports and premises
text: Four statements are carried as premises. H1 and H2 are this paper's names for two of T12's ingredients used off dimension four; Hypothesis (S) is T12's; U is this paper's transposition rule.

title: Setting, imports and premises
Constituents, momentum and where mass begins
text: The commutant of the spin action is the commutant of the even algebra, since the bivectors generate $\Cl^{0}$ as an algebra; so U1's field and the field of this definition agree. The constructions are explicit: $e_{t}e_{a}$ squares to $+1$, and $\Cl^{0}(V)f$ has real dimension $2$, $4$, $8$ in dimensions three, four, five, which is minimal (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}); $\hf$ is a product of two or three commuting factors $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 + b)$ with $b$ an even blade of square $+1$. The script builds both by a search over commuting even blades (Part A).

title: The constituent's field in each tower
text:
In tower $r$ the fields $\F(T)$ and $\F(S)$ are equal, and equal to the division algebra of residue $r + 1$:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccccccc@{}}
\toprule
$r$ & $6$ & $2$ & $1$ & $7$ & $3$ & $5$ & $0$ & $4$ \\
tower & $(1,3)$ & $(3,1)$ & $(2,1)$ & $(1,2)$ & $(4,1)$ & $(1,4)$ & $(2,2)$ & $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$ \\
conformal & $(2,4)$ & $(4,2)$ & $(3,2)$ & $(2,3)$ & $(5,2)$ & $(2,5)$ & $(3,3)$ & $(5,1)$, $(1,5)$ \\
field & $\C$ & $\C$ & $\R$ & $\R$ & $\HH$ & $\HH$ & $\R$ & $\HH$ \\
$\dim_{\R} T$, $\dim_{\R} S$ & $8, 4$ & $8, 4$ & $4, 2$ & $4, 2$ & $16, 8$ & $16, 8$ & $4, 2$ & $8, 4$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
In particular the field is not a function of the conformal pseudoscalar's square: $Q(\omega) = -1$ at $r = 7$ (field $\R$) and at $r = 3$ (field $\HH$).
proof:
\textit{The two even algebras.}\enspace By Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(i),
\begin{align*}
\Cl^{0}(\hatV) &= \Cl^{0}(p+1, q+1) \cong \Cl(p+1, q), \\
\Cl^{0}(V) &= \Cl^{0}(p, q) \cong \Cl(p, q-1),
\end{align*}
and both have residue $(p+1) - q = p - (q-1) = r + 1$. The one tower with $q = 0$ is $(4,0)$: there $\Cl^{0}(4,0) \cong \Cl(0,3)$, of residue $-3 \equiv 5 = r + 1$, and $(0,4)$ gives the same algebra.



\emph{The commutant.}  By Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(ii) each algebra is a matrix algebra over the division algebra $D(r+1)$, or a sum of two copies of one, and by Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(iii) the commutant of a minimal left ideal is $D(r+1)$. Reading $D$ off for each tower:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
r & 6 & 2 & 1 & 7 & 3 & 5 & 0 & 4 \\
r + 1 & 7 & 3 & 2 & 0 & 4 & 6 & 1 & 5 \\ \hline
D(r+1) & \C & \C & \R & \R & \HH & \HH & \R & \HH
\end{array}
\]



\emph{Checks.}  The script computes every commutant from scratch on exact matrix representations of the ideals and classifies it (checks A1, A2), with the dimensions (A3) and the pseudoscalars (A4, A5).

title: Constituents, momentum and where mass begins
Ideals, fields and momentum
text:
Let $\hf$ be a primitive idempotent of $\Cl^{0}(\hatV)$, and in a causal tower let $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$ for a space direction $e_{a}$, which is a primitive idempotent of $\Cl^{0}(V)$ in dimensions three to five (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}); in the sterile towers $f$ is any primitive idempotent of $\Cl^{0}(V)$. The \emph{constituent ideal} is $T = \Cl^{0}(\hatV)\hf$ and the \emph{spinor ideal} is $S = \Cl^{0}(V)f$. Their \emph{fields} are the commutants $\F(T) = \mathrm{End}_{\Cl^{0}(\hatV)}(T)$ and $\F(S) = \mathrm{End}_{\Cl^{0}(V)}(S)$, the latter realised as right multiplication by the corner algebra $f\Cl^{0}(V)f$. In a causal tower the \emph{adjoint} is $x^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{x}e_{t}^{-1}$, and the \emph{momentum} of $\psi \in S$ is
\[
j(\psi) \;=\; \ip{\psi e_{t} \rev{\psi}}_{1}.
\]
The total momentum of constituents $\psi_{1}, \ldots, \psi_{n}$ is $P = \sum_{i} j(\psi_{i})$, and its \emph{squared mass} is $m^{2} = Q(e_{t})\,Q(P)$.

title: T14's types are a different commutant
text: T14's Theorem 3.4 assigns real type to $r = 1, 2$, complex type with an intrinsic $U(1)$ to $r = 3, 7$, and quaternionic type to $r = 4, 5, 6$ \cite[Thm.~3.4]{ButlerT14}. That is the commutant of the full Clifford algebra $\Cl(V)$ on its irreducible module; Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} is the commutant of the spin action on the constituent ideal. Both are correct and they answer different questions. T14's intrinsic $U(1)$ at $r = 3$ and $r = 7$ is the central pseudoscalar, which reappears here as structure the tower carries beside its constituent field: at $r = 7$ as a unit joining two real constituents (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit}), at $r = 3$ as the unit $I_{7}$ inside the quaternions (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions}).

title: The adjoint and the norm of the field
proof:
\textit{(i) The blades.}\enspace Every direction other than $e_{t}$ has square $-Q(e_{t})$. There are two cases.

If $t \notin K$, moving $e_{t}$ through the $|K|$ vectors of $\rev{e_{K}}$ costs one sign each, and a blade times its reverse is the product of its squares:
\[
e_{K}^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{e_{K}}e_{t}^{-1} = (-1)^{|K|}\rev{e_{K}}, \qquad e_{K}\rev{e_{K}} = \bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|},
\]
so $e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{|K|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K|} = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}$.

If $e_{K} = e_{t}e_{K'}$, then $\rev{e_{K}} = \rev{e_{K'}}e_{t}$, and
\begin{align*}
e_{K}^{\dagger} &= e_{t}\rev{e_{K'}} = (-1)^{|K'|}\,\rev{e_{K'}}\,e_{t}, \\
e_{K}e_{K}^{\dagger} &= (-1)^{|K'|}\,e_{t}\bigl(e_{K'}\rev{e_{K'}}\bigr)e_{t} = (-1)^{|K'|}\bigl(-Q(e_{t})\bigr)^{|K'|}\,Q(e_{t}) = Q(e_{t})^{|K|}.
\end{align*}
For $K \neq L$, $e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}$ is a multiple of $e_{K \triangle L}$, which has no scalar part. Hence for even $x = \sum_{K}x_{K}e_{K}$,
\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K,L}x_{K}x_{L}\,\ip{e_{K}e_{L}^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; \sum_{K}x_{K}^{2} \qquad \text{(check B0)}.
\]



\emph{(ii) The corner and its conjugation.}  With $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$ and $\rev{(e_{t}e_{a})} = e_{a}e_{t}$,
\[
f^{\dagger} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + e_{t}\,e_{a}e_{t}\,e_{t}^{-1}\bigr) = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + e_{t}e_{a}) = f.
\]
The corner $\F = f\Cl^{0}f$ is a division algebra $\R$, $\C$ or $\HH$ with unit $f$ (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}(iii)). It is closed under $\dagger$, since $(fxf)^{\dagger} = fx^{\dagger}f$, and $\dagger$ is an anti-involution of it with $\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} > 0$ for $x \neq 0$ by (i).

The standard conjugation is the only anti-involution with that positivity. Every other candidate has an element with $xx^{\dagger} = -f$, whose scalar part is $-\tfrac{1}{2}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item on $\C$ the other candidate is the identity, and a unit square root $x$ of $-f$ gives $xx^{\dagger} = xx = -f$;
\item on $\HH$ every other anti-involution is $x \mapsto u\bar{x}u^{-1}$ for a unit imaginary $u$, and a unit imaginary $v$ anticommuting with $u$ gives $v\,u\bar{v}u^{-1} = v^{2} = -f$.
\end{itemize}
So $\dagger$ is the standard conjugation, and
\[
x^{\dagger}x \;=\; xx^{\dagger} \;=\; N(x)\,f
\]
with $N$ the standard norm; the script verifies this as a polynomial identity in $x$'s coordinates (check B1). Taking scalar parts, with $\ip{f}_{0} = \tfrac{1}{2}$,
\[
\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0} \;=\; N(x)\,\ip{f}_{0} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,N(x),
\]
which is positive definite by (i), since $x$ is even (B3).



\emph{(iii) The norm law.}  By the definition of the adjoint, $e_{t}\rev{x} = x^{\dagger}e_{t}$, and $\psi f = \psi$ for $\psi \in S$. So
\begin{align*}
\psi x\,e_{t}\,\rev{(\psi x)} &= \psi\,\bigl(x e_{t}\rev{x}\bigr)\,\rev{\psi} \\
&= \psi\,\bigl(xx^{\dagger}\bigr)\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\
&= N(x)\,\psi f\,e_{t}\rev{\psi} \\
&= N(x)\,\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi},
\end{align*}
and the grade-one part is $j(\psi x) = N(x)\,j(\psi)$ (B2).

title: Where mass begins in each causal tower
text:
Let $\psi, \psi_{1}, \psi_{2} \in S$ in a causal tower of dimension $n$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $n = 3$ and $n = 4$ the reversion pairing is alternating, $\rev{\psi}\psi = 0$, every single constituent's momentum is null, and
\[
m^{2}\bigl(j(\psi_{1}) + j(\psi_{2})\bigr) \;=\; 2\,\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}, \qquad x = \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}.
\]
Mass begins at two constituents; it vanishes exactly when $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2} = 0$.
\item[(ii)] For $n = 5$ the reversion pairing is not alternating, and
\[
m^{2}\bigl(j(\psi)\bigr) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\ip{xx^{\dagger}}_{0}, \qquad x = \rev{\psi}\psi,
\]
which vanishes on a nonzero proper cone in $S$. Mass begins at one constituent.
\end{enumerate}
In every causal tower the total momentum of any number of constituents is timelike or null, never spacelike.
proof:
\textit{The pairing as a sandwich.}\enspace Write $\psi = \phi f$ with $\phi \in \Cl^{0}(V)$ and $f = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + b)$, $b$ a bivector of square $+1$. Then $\rev{b} = -b$, so $\rev{f} = 1 - f$ and
\[
\rev{\psi}\psi \;=\; (1 - f)\;\rev{\phi}\phi\;f.
\]
The element $\rev{\phi}\phi$ is even and reversion-invariant, so it has grades $0$ and $4$ only:
\[
\rev{\phi}\phi = s + F, \qquad s = \ip{\rev{\phi}\phi}_{0}, \quad F = \ip{\rev{\phi}\phi}_{4}.
\]
Since $(1 - f)f = 0$, every part of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ that commutes with $b$ drops out of the sandwich:
\[
(1 - f)\,c\,f \;=\; c\,(1 - f)f \;=\; 0 \qquad \text{whenever } cb = bc.
\]



\emph{Dimensions three and four.}  In dimension three $F = 0$. In dimension four $F = uI$ is a multiple of the pseudoscalar, which commutes with every even element and in particular with $b$. In both cases all of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ commutes with $b$, so $\rev{\psi}\psi = 0$. This is the alternation in (i).



\emph{Dimension five.}  Here $F$ is a general four-vector, which need not commute with $b$, and $(1 - f)\,F f \neq 0$ for suitable $\phi$, so the pairing is not alternating.



\emph{The mass laws.}  The two displayed laws are identities between polynomials of degree four in the coordinates of $\psi_{1}, \psi_{2}$ (respectively $\psi$) on a basis of $S$. The script verifies them as polynomial identities over $\mathbb{Q}$, not on samples, in all six causal towers (checks B4, B5), together with the nullity of $j(\psi)$ in dimensions three and four (B4); it exhibits a nonzero $\psi$ with $\rev{\psi}\psi = 0$ in each five-dimensional tower (B6). The right-hand sides are nonnegative by Lemma \claimref{dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm}(i), so each single momentum (and in dimensions three and four each pair sum) is timelike or null.



\emph{Any number of constituents.}  For every $\psi \in S$,
\begin{align*}
Q(e_{t})\,\bigl(j(\psi)\cdot e_{t}\bigr) &= Q(e_{t})\,\ip{\psi e_{t}\rev{\psi}\,e_{t}}_{0} \\
&= \ip{\psi\,e_{t}\rev{\psi}e_{t}^{-1}}_{0} \\
&= \ip{\psi\psi^{\dagger}}_{0} \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \text{(B7)}.
\end{align*}
So every constituent's momentum is causal and lies in the same closed half-space bounded by $e_{t}^{\perp}$, hence in the same half of the causal cone, and that half is closed under addition.

title: The four-dimensional case is T11's formula
text: In this tower $x = \rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$ lies in the two-dimensional space $(1-f)\Cl^{0}f$, a copy of $\C$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i) is T11's two-constituent mass formula \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT11} written in the even algebra, the pairing $x$ playing the role of the bracket. In five dimensions the law is the classical Fierz identity of a single Dirac spinor, which in geometric algebra says that the four-vector part of $\rev{\phi}\phi$ survives the idempotent.

title: The momentum-preserving mixings of constituents
text: Let $\F = f\Cl^{0}(V)f$ act on $S$ on the right and on $S^{n}$ by $\psi'_{i} = \sum_{k}\psi_{k}U_{ki}$ for $U \in M_{n}(\F)$. Then $U$ preserves the total momentum of every $n$-tuple if and only if $UU^{\dagger} = 1$, where $(U^{\dagger})_{ik} = (U_{ki})^{\dagger}$. The momentum-preserving group is $O(n)$, $U(n)$ or $Sp(n)$ as $\F = \R$, $\C$, $\HH$: $O(n)$ in the three-dimensional towers, $U(n)$ in this tower and the mirror, $Sp(n)$ in the five-dimensional towers.
proof:
\textit{Unitary mixings preserve the momentum.}\enspace Using $e_{t}\rev{y} = y^{\dagger}e_{t}$ on each entry of $U$,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{i}\psi'_{i}e_{t}\rev{\psi'_{i}} &= \sum_{i}\sum_{k,l}\psi_{k}U_{ki}\,e_{t}\,\rev{U_{li}}\,\rev{\psi_{l}} \\
&= \sum_{k,l}\psi_{k}\Bigl(\sum_{i}U_{ki}U_{li}^{\dagger}\Bigr)e_{t}\rev{\psi_{l}}.
\end{align*}
If $UU^{\dagger} = 1$, that is $\sum_{i}U_{ki}U_{li}^{\dagger} = \delta_{kl}f$, the right-hand side is $\sum_{k}\psi_{k}e_{t}\rev{\psi_{k}}$.



\emph{Only unitary mixings do.}  Take $\psi_{k} = \psi a_{k}$ for one $\psi \in S$ with $j(\psi) \neq 0$ and a row $a = (a_{k}) \in \F^{n}$. Then $\psi'_{i} = \psi\,(aU)_{i}$, and Lemma \claimref{dark-tower-matter.adjoint-norm}(iii) gives the total momenta before and after as
\[
P = \Bigl(\sum_{k}N(a_{k})\Bigr)\,j(\psi), \qquad P' = \Bigl(\sum_{i}N\bigl((aU)_{i}\bigr)\Bigr)\,j(\psi).
\]
Their equality for every $a$ says that $U$ preserves the positive definite form $\sum_{k}N(a_{k})$ on $\F^{n}$, whose polarisation is the standard $\F$-Hermitian form; so $UU^{\dagger} = 1$.



\emph{The groups.}  The isometry groups of the standard forms over $\R$, $\C$, $\HH$ are $O(n)$, $U(n)$, $Sp(n)$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} assigns the fields. The script checks an $\F$-unitary mixing in every causal tower as a polynomial identity (C1) and exhibits a non-unitary mixing that changes the total momentum (C2).

title: The ladder pairs and the complex unit
text: A \emph{ladder pair} is a pair $w, v$ of null vectors of the conformal space, $Q(w) = Q(v) = 0$, or of vectors dressed by a complex unit with $w^{2} = v^{2} = 0$, such that $wv + vw = 1$: the canonical anticommutation relations, one fermionic mode per pair \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT3}. Pairs built from real hyperbolic planes of $\hatV$ need no unit; their number is the real Witt index $\min(p,q) + 1$. The constituent's pair count is the complex Witt index $\lfloor (n+2)/2 \rfloor$ (T12's Lemma 2.12 in even dimension \cite[Lem.~2.12]{ButlerT12}; in odd dimension the same bound, with one generator left over).

title: The ladder pairs of the causal towers
proof:
In a causal tower $\min(p,q) = 1$, and $\hatV$ has signature $(p+1, q+1)$. Its Witt indices are
\[
\text{real: } \min(p+1, q+1) = 2, \qquad
\text{complex: } \Bigl\lfloor \frac{\dim\hatV}{2} \Bigr\rfloor =
\begin{cases} 2, & \dim\hatV = 5, \\ 3, & \dim\hatV = 6, 7. \end{cases}
\]
Check D1 builds the two real pairs of $\Cl(3,2)$ and $\Cl(2,3)$ on their modules and verifies the relations. In this tower and the mirror the field of (ii) is $\C$ by Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}.

title: The third pair's unit in five dimensions
proof:
\textit{(i) The unit $I_{7}$.}\enspace $I_{7}$ is central in $\Cl(5,2)$ (odd dimension) with $Q(I_{7}) = -1$ (the section ``Setting, imports and premises''). Central elements commute with the spin action, so $I_{7} \in \HH$, the spin commutant of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}. Take $Q(e_{a}) = Q(e_{b}) = +1$ and
\[
w = \tfrac{1}{2}(e_{a} + I_{7}e_{b}), \qquad \bar{w} = \tfrac{1}{2}(e_{a} - I_{7}e_{b}).
\]
Since $I_{7}$ commutes with vectors and $e_{a}e_{b} = -e_{b}e_{a}$,
\begin{align*}
w^{2} &= \tfrac{1}{4}\bigl(Q(e_{a}) + I_{7}^{2}\,Q(e_{b})\bigr) = \tfrac{1}{4}(1 - 1) = 0, \\
w\bar{w} + \bar{w}w &= \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(Q(e_{a}) - I_{7}^{2}\,Q(e_{b})\bigr) = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 + 1) = 1.
\end{align*}
The cross relations with the real pairs hold because distinct basis vectors anticommute and $I_{7}$ commutes with them (D3). Closure and the centraliser are computed (D4, D5).



\emph{(ii) A unit anticommuting with $I_{7}$.}  $J$ commutes with the even algebra (it lies in the spin commutant) and anticommutes with $I_{7}$. Every vector factors as $e = (eI_{7}^{-1})\,I_{7}$ with $eI_{7}^{-1}$ even, so
\[
JeJ^{-1} \;=\; (eI_{7}^{-1})\,\bigl(JI_{7}J^{-1}\bigr) \;=\; (eI_{7}^{-1})(-I_{7}) \;=\; -e \qquad \text{(D6)}.
\]
Hence $J(I_{7}e_{b})J^{-1} = I_{7}e_{b}$ and
\[
Jw_{3}J^{-1} \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}(e_{a} - I_{7}e_{b}) \;=\; -\bar{w}_{3},
\]
and the closure has dimension $30$ (D7).



\emph{(iii) The residue-five tower.}  The centre of $\HH$ is $\R$ and $Q(\omega) = +1$ (A4), so the algebra names no unit. The spin and Clifford commutants coincide on this module (D8), so every unit $u \in \HH$ commutes with the vectors. With $Q(e_{a}) = Q(e_{b}) = -1$ and $u^{2} = -1$,
\[
w_{3}v_{3} + v_{3}w_{3} \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(Q(e_{a}) - u^{2}\,Q(e_{b})\bigr) \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}(-1 - 1) \;=\; 1 \qquad \text{(D9 to D11)}.
\]
For the conjugacy, with $u^{2} = u'^{2} = -1$,
\begin{align*}
(1 - u'u)\,u &= u - u'u^{2} = u + u', \\
u'\,(1 - u'u) &= u' - u'^{2}u = u' + u,
\end{align*}
so the two sides agree, and $1 - u'u = 0$ only at $u' = -u$ (D12).

title: The ladder pairs and the complex unit
The two readings of the unit
text: Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions} is where the two five-dimensional towers part. At $r = 3$ the unit that builds the pairs is fixed by the algebra, and the quaternionic unit group of a single constituent, which preserves its momentum (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}), does not preserve the pair structure. At $r = 5$ every choice of unit is equivalent, and each choice cuts the quaternionic group to the circle it generates. Under U3 both towers therefore build their pairs with one complex unit; they differ in whether the algebra names it. With an external unit, which commutes with the whole quaternionic group, the group survives in both towers alike (Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.branches-break-u-what-they-give}).

title: The gauge algebras of the odd towers
proof:
\textit{(i) The two factors.}\enspace The constituent count is two (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i)) and the field is $\R$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}), so by U2 (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}) the slot group is $O(2)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}). The pairs are real (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.pairs}(i)), and by U2 their group is the orthogonal group of the real pair space, again $O(2)$.

The norm clause of U2 matters here. Without it, the pair mixings preserving the canonical relations alone would be $GL(2,\R)$, acting by $B$ on the $w_{i}$ and by $B^{-T}$ on the $v_{i}$. That is the mechanism of Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.kleinian-algebra}, where the sterile tower has no time direction and so no adjoint.



\emph{(i) The kernel.}  An automorphism of $\R^{2} \otimes \R^{2}$ respecting both factors is $A \otimes B$, and
\[
A \otimes B = 1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A = \lambda 1, \;\; B = \lambda^{-1}1,
\]
with $\lambda$ real and orthogonal, so $\lambda = \pm 1$. The kernel $\{(1,1), (-1,-1)\}$ is discrete, no generator is lost, and the algebra is $\so(2) \oplus \so(2)$ (the gauge algebra by \claimref{dark-tower-matter.h2-identification}; checks E1, E2).



\emph{(i) The charges.}  Write $s$ and $p$ for the weights of the slot and pair rotations. The element $(-1, -1)$ acts as $(-1)^{s + p}$, so the group's representations are those with $s + p$ even, on which
\[
q_{\pm} = \frac{s \pm p}{2}
\]
are the integral charges of $U(1)_{\pm}$ (F2).



\emph{(ii) The slot.}  The constituent count is one (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(ii)). The slot group of one constituent is $Sp(1)$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.ladder}), acting on the spinor part through H1 (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.h1-momentum})'s identification of the two fields. The pair unit of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions} lies in that field, and only the circle it generates commutes with the pair algebra, so the slot is one complex line with group $U(1)$.



\emph{(ii) The pairs and the kernel.}  By U2 the three complex pairs carry $U(3)$. The action $(\lambda, B) \mapsto \lambda B$ has the common scalar as its kernel, as in T12's proof of its Theorem 4.1, so the group is
\[
\frac{U(1) \times U(3)}{U(1)} \;\cong\; U(3)
\]
(E3; the control $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3} \mapsto 12$ is E4).

title: The gauge algebras
text: In the mirror the algebra and global form are this tower's, $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ and $S(U(2) \times U(3))$: that is T14's copy theorem (\claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), which Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirror-algebra} below realises as an explicit isomorphism of the even algebras.

title: The gauge algebras
Branches that break U, and what they give
text: Two transpositions reproduce this tower and break a clause of Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}. (a) Counting the $r = 7$ constituent in the full Clifford module, where the central $\omega$ joins two real constituents into one complex element that is already massive (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}(i) for the two real parts), gives the hierarchy $\C^{1} \otimes \C^{2}$ and $\uu(2)$, with content a doublet of $Y = \tfrac{1}{2}$, a singlet of $Y = -1$ and a neutral singlet; it breaks U1, since $\omega$ is odd and does not act on the spin-irreducible ideal (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit}(ii)). (b) Building the five-dimensional third pair with an external unit, one adjoined from outside the real algebra, which commutes with the quaternionic unit group, keeps that group as the slot group of the one constituent: the hierarchy is a quaternionic line tensor $\C^{3}$, with automorphisms $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ and global form $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, and vector-like content $(2,3)_{1/6}$, $(2,1)_{-1/2}$. It keeps U1 and U2 and breaks U3; it is T12's own practice of working in the complexification, carried to a tower whose field is $\HH$; and it is open at $r = 3$ and $r = 5$ on the same terms, so it does not separate them. Its $\su(2)$ acts on one constituent's quaternionic multiplicity, not on two constituents. Their arithmetic is in the supplementary scripts (\file{D3C}, \file{D5Q}; the section ``Machine verification''). Neither is a result of this paper.

title: Content
text: T12's lesson is that fermions are generators of the composite, not its states \cite[Rem.~5.2, Prop.~5.3]{ButlerT12}. The generators of a hierarchy $\F^{m} \otimes \F^{k}$ are its single slot-pair cells; Hypothesis (S) adds the constituent-level states.

title: The three-dimensional towers' content
text:
In the towers $r = 1, 7$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The generators are the four cells of $\R^{2} \otimes \R^{2}$, of weights $(s, p) \in \{\pm 1\}^{2}$; as complex two-component fermions they are $A$, with $(q_{+}, q_{-}) = (1, 0)$, and $B$, with $(0, 1)$, and their conjugates. Each is charged under one factor only: the tower is two copies of single-flavour electrodynamics in $2+1$ dimensions, exchanged by the pair reflection $p \mapsto -p$.
\item[(ii)] Every weight of the exterior algebra of the cells has $s + p$ even; no state of the tensor state space has weight $(\pm 1, 0)$ or $(0, \pm 1)$.
\item[(iii)] Under (S) the constituent-level states have weight $(\pm 1, 0)$, off the lattice $s + p$ even: (S) and the global form of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras}(i) are incompatible. Of the directions the transport adds, the rung directions carry $(\pm 1, 0)$ and the pair directions $(0, \pm 1)$, and both are excluded; the one neutral direction (the leftover generator of the odd conformal algebra) is allowed, and its value is a bare mass. The tower has no charged Higgs analogue.
\item[(iv)] There is no chirality: the odd-dimensional modules carry no Lorentz-invariant grading \cite[Prop.~3.9]{ButlerT14}. Gauge-invariant Dirac masses exist for $A$ and $B$ without any condensate, and there is no baryon-like composite: every gauge-neutral state has zero net number of each cell.
\end{enumerate}
proof:
\textit{(i)}\enspace The cells are single-occupation states. The charges $q_{\pm} = (s \pm p)/2$ of the $U(1)_{+} \times U(1)_{-}$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras}(i) send
\[
(s, p) = (1, 1) \;\mapsto\; (q_{+}, q_{-}) = (1, 0), \qquad (1, -1) \;\mapsto\; (0, 1) \qquad \text{(F2)},
\]
and the pair reflection $p \mapsto -p$ exchanges them.



\emph{(ii)}  A product of cells adds weights, and each cell has $s + p \in \{-2, 0, 2\}$ (F1).



\emph{(iii)}  A constituent-level state occupies one slot mode and no pair mode, so its weight is $(\pm 1, 0)$, off the lattice $s + p$ even (Remark \claimref{note.dark-tower-matter.why-s-fails-three-dimensions-not}). The weights of the transported directions are computed in the supplementary script \file{D3R} (checks H5 to H9): rung directions $(\pm 1, 0)$, pair directions $(0, \pm 1)$, the leftover generator $(0,0)$.



\emph{(iv)}  This is the odd case of T14's Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}. A mass term $\bar{A}A$ has weight zero, and a neutral product of cells pairs each cell with its conjugate.

title: The neutral row
text: In a hierarchy $\C^{1} \otimes \C^{k}$ whose central generator acts by $k$ on the slot and $-1$ on each pair, the state with the slot and all $k$ pairs occupied has weight $k - k = 0$. The constituent-level generator of a one-constituent hierarchy is therefore neutral: the trace-free central generator of $\uu(1) \oplus \uu(k)$ on $\C^{1} \oplus \C^{k}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors) is $(k\,I_{4}, -I_{4}\,1_{k})$ up to scale, and weights add. In the five-dimensional towers the pairs themselves are built with the unit $u$ of the hierarchy's scalars $\mathrm{span}\{1, u\}$ ($u = I_{7}$, the pseudoscalar of $\Cl(5,2)$, at $r = 3$; a chosen unit of $\HH$ at $r = 5$; Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions}); here $I_{4}$ is the unit of the multiplicity spaces only, and the two are not identified. Arithmetic.

title: The five-dimensional towers' content
text:
In the towers $r = 3, 5$, under (S) the state space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{1} \oplus \C^{3})$ has sixteen states. With $Y = s - k/3$ ($s$ the slot occupation, $k$ the number of occupied pairs), the complement $(s,k) \mapsto (1-s, 3-k)$ negates $Y$ and conjugates colour, so the sixteen are eight species-states and their conjugates, four vector-like Dirac species:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccl@{}}
\toprule
species & colour & $Y$ & states $(s,k)$ \\

These are the electric charges of one of our generations with the weak doublet removed. Through the section $B \mapsto ((\det B)^{-1}, B)$ the centre of $U(3)$ acts on $(s,k)$ by $\lambda^{k - 3s} = \lambda^{-3Y}$, so $3Y$ is an integer with $3Y + k \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, $k$ being the triality: the lattice of $U(3)$, satisfied automatically; the neutral species $N$ is the empty state and the full row of Remark \ref{lem:neutralrow}. Without (S) the content is one Dirac colour triplet of $Y = 2/3$. There is no chirality and every species has a gauge-invariant bare mass.
proof:
The state space under (S) (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.hypothesis-s-slot-statistics}) has
\[
\dim \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{4} \;=\; \sum_{s=0}^{1}\sum_{k=0}^{3}\binom{3}{k} \;=\; 2 \cdot 8 \;=\; 16
\]
states, the $\binom{3}{k}$ states at pair number $k$ forming the $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$ of the $SU(3)$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras}(ii). The complement negates $Y$:
\[
Y(1 - s, 3 - k) \;=\; (1 - s) - \frac{3 - k}{3} \;=\; -\Bigl(s - \frac{k}{3}\Bigr) \;=\; -Y(s, k),
\]
and the remaining weights are arithmetic (F3, F4). The masses are as in Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(iv).

title: Content
Why (S) fails in three dimensions, not five
text: In both cases the slot-level states are charged under the kernel of the action on the hierarchy. In five dimensions the kernel is the common scalar $U(1)$, and the subgroup $S(U(1) \times U(3)) = \{((\det B)^{-1}, B)\}$ maps isomorphically onto the quotient $U(3)$: the exterior algebra of slot and pair modes is a representation of that section, as T12 uses $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ in four dimensions. In three dimensions the kernel $\{\pm(1,1)\}$ is discrete inside the torus $SO(2) \times SO(2)$, and no subgroup maps isomorphically onto the quotient, so the slot-level states are not representations of the global form. Under (S) the five-dimensional state space has a tenth abelian automorphism, the slot number, beyond the nine of $\uu(3)$; this paper takes it as a global symmetry, not gauged (a choice: T12 counts the corresponding extra generator in four dimensions and finds it anomaly-free, broken by the right-handed neutrino's Majorana mass \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT12}); here it is broken only by a mass term for $N$ off the pair unit's axis.

title: Chern-Simons levels of the odd towers' content
proof:
\textit{(i)}\enspace With bare level $k$ and one unit-charge fermion of mass $m$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}(i)), the effective level is, by Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-parity-anomaly},
\[
k_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; k + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{sign}(m) \;\in\; \mathbb{Z} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k \in \mathbb{Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \qquad \text{(G1, G2)},
\]
and no half-integer is zero, so a parity-odd Chern-Simons term is always present.



\emph{(ii)}  In units $q' = 3Y$ the species of Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content} carry $q' = 2, -1, -3, 0$ for $U, D, E, N$, with colour multiplicity $3$ for $U$ and $D$. So
\begin{align*}
\sum q'^{3} &= 3(2)^{3} + 3(-1)^{3} + (-3)^{3} + 0 = 24 - 3 - 27 = -6, \\
\sum q' &= 3(2) + 3(-1) + (-3) + 0 = 0 \qquad \text{(G3)}.
\end{align*}
In the induced coefficient $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum \mathrm{sign}(m)\,q'^{3}$ (Fact \claimref{rule2.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-shift}) the terms of $U$ and $N$ are the integers $\pm 12$ and $0$, and those of $D$ and $E$ are $\pm\tfrac{3}{2}$ and $\pm\tfrac{27}{2}$, whose sum is an integer for each choice of signs.

title: The paired towers
text: T14's indifference premise P2 equates the data of the two members of each reversal pair, $\{2, 6\}$, $\{1, 7\}$ and $\{3, 5\}$ \cite[Prem.~2.2]{ButlerT14}. This section compares the members of the odd pairs as algebras.

title: The central unit of the residue-seven tower
proof:
\textit{(i)}\enspace By the formula of the section ``Setting, imports and premises'' (\claimref{primer.sign}), $Q(\omega) = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$. Each rung adds $(1,1)$ to the signature, so $n$ rises by two and $q$ by one, and the first exponent changes by
\[
\frac{(n+2)(n+1)}{2} - \frac{n(n-1)}{2} \;=\; 2n + 1,
\]
which is odd. The two sign changes cancel, so $Q(\omega)$ is constant along each tower and equal to its value at the first rung:
\[
Q(\omega_{2,3}) = (-1)^{10}(-1)^{3} = -1, \qquad Q(\omega_{3,2}) = (-1)^{10}(-1)^{2} = +1.
\]
Every rung has odd dimension, so $\omega$ is central (H1, H2; \claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}).



\emph{(ii)}  $\omega$ is a product of five vectors (H3), so it is odd, left multiplication by it exchanges the even and odd parts, and $\hat{\omega} = (-1)^{5}\omega = -\omega$ (\claimref{std-algebra.involution-properties}).



\emph{(iii)}  $\omega$ is central with $\omega^{2} = -1$ (H4), so $c + s\omega$ commutes with the Clifford action, and for $X, Y \in T$
\[
(c + s\omega)(X + \omega Y) \;=\; cX + s\omega^{2}Y + \omega(sX + cY) \;=\; (cX - sY) + \omega(sX + cY).
\]

title: Paired towers hold the same kind of matter
text:
Under H2 and Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule} the two towers of each odd dimension have the same constituent field, the same mass onset, the same gauge algebra and the same content. They differ only as follows.

\midrule

\midrule

proof:
The shared rows are Theorems \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.where-mass-begins}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.gauge-algebras} and Propositions \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content}, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content}. The differing rows come from Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit} and Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions}, except two that are computed in supplementary scripts: the slot-reflection row in \file{D3C} (Part I), and the invariant-form row in the referee script \file{CHECK\_ALG/check\_r3\_r5.py}.

The argument holds given \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}, which fixes the constituent field and the slot and pair groups, and \claimref{dark-tower-matter.h2-identification}, which identifies the gauge algebra with the automorphism algebra of the minimal massive hierarchy.

title: The paired towers
The $r = 5$ unit: datum or field
text: If the unit $u$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.third-pairs-unit-five-dimensions}(iii) is a constant of the tower, every choice gives an isomorphic tower and nothing observable distinguishes it from $r = 3$; this is how this tower treats its own unit, which the algebra fixes up to sign. If $u$ varies over spacetime, the tower carries a sigma model on $S^{2}$ with two massless five-dimensional scalars, which moves the radiation bound of Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(iii) from $0.085$ to $0.084$. The series supplies no kinetic term for $u$; the first reading is this tower's.

title: The mirror's even algebra as a real isomorphism
proof:
\textit{(i) The product rule.}\enspace Write $Q$ for the squares of the first signature and $Q' = -Q$ for those of the second. For even blades $e_{K}$, $e_{L}$,
\[
e_{K}e_{L} \;=\; \sigma \prod_{c \in K \cap L}Q(e_{c})\;e_{K \triangle L},
\]
with $\sigma$ the reordering sign, which does not depend on the squares; the same holds in the second algebra with $Q'$ in place of $Q$.



\emph{(i) The map respects it.}  Let $\varphi(e_{K}) = (-1)^{|K|/2}e_{K}$, and use $|K \triangle L| = |K| + |L| - 2|K \cap L|$ and $\prod_{c}Q'(e_{c}) = (-1)^{|K \cap L|}\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})$. Then
\begin{align*}
\varphi(e_{K}e_{L}) &= \sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,(-1)^{|K \triangle L|/2}\,e_{K \triangle L}
= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}(-1)^{|K \cap L|}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}, \\
\varphi(e_{K})\,\varphi(e_{L}) &= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q'(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}
= (-1)^{\frac{|K|+|L|}{2}}(-1)^{|K \cap L|}\,\sigma\prod_{c}Q(e_{c})\,e_{K \triangle L}.
\end{align*}
The two agree. The script checks every pair of basis blades in both cases (I1).



\emph{(ii)}  On the pseudoscalars,
\[
\varphi(I_{4}') = (-1)^{4/2}\,I_{4} = +I_{4}, \qquad \varphi(I_{6}') = (-1)^{6/2}\,I_{6} = -I_{6} \qquad \text{(I2)}.
\]



\emph{(iii)}  The commutants are $\HH$ and $\R$ (I3; Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}).

title: The mirror
text: So the mirror's constituents are complex, as ours are (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}): its real (Majorana) ground spinors do not make them real. The isomorphism sends the mirror's field unit $I_{4}'$ to ours and its conformal unit $I_{6}'$ to minus ours. If each tower's constituent unit is taken to be its own oriented conformal pseudoscalar, the mirror's constituent unit and field unit therefore have the opposite relative sign to ours, and the mirror is the parity image of this tower. That reading is interpretive and depends on the identification of the transported plane, which with one sign reversed would flip the sign of $I_{6}'$'s image. Nothing gravitational distinguishes the two.

title: The mirror
The mirror's temperature and premise P2
text: T14 applies P2 along the reversal orbit to equate the ceiling coupling and the asymmetry per mode, both data of the descent \cite[Thm.~4.3(iv), (v)]{ButlerT14}. The energy the descent deposits per unit charge is a datum of the same kind, and P2 declares which of $2$, $6$ is visible to be indexical. Applied with the same reach, P2 gives $\xi = T'/T = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = \tfrac{8}{7}(\tfrac{11}{4})^{4/3} + 3.044 = 7.45$ at recombination, excluded by a factor of about $25$. T14's mirror, cold from the gravitational floor upward \cite[Prop.~4.6, Prop.~A.2]{ButlerT14}, is therefore an exception to P2 that T14 neither states nor costs. It is an exception at P2's version-1 reach, the reach T14 used; P2 as scoped (version 2) leaves $\xi$ free (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}), and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}). Assembly level.
proof:
\textit{The reach of P2.}\enspace The equalities of T14's Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), as T14 states them (the theorem's version 8; at its current version (iv) is the common-ceiling-coupling premise and (v) reads P2 on the stored charge), rest on P2's clause that a difference between two continuous data of one reversal orbit is an uncaused distinction. T14's Proposition A.2 (\claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature}) calls what the descent deposited ``a datum, not a computation'', and T14's Proposition 4.6 (\claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) carries the mirror's temperature as such a datum, from the floor up to the $\Neff$ cap.



\emph{The number.}  At $\xi = 1$ the mirror is a full Standard-Model copy at the photon temperature. Its energy density is that of a photon, worth $\tfrac{8}{7}(\tfrac{11}{4})^{4/3}$ neutrino species, plus three neutrinos:
\[
\Delta\Neff \;=\; \underbrace{\tfrac{8}{7}\bigl(\tfrac{11}{4}\bigr)^{4/3}}_{\text{mirror photon}} \;+\; \underbrace{3.044}_{\text{mirror neutrinos}} \;=\; 4.40 + 3.044 \;=\; 7.45 \qquad \text{(K2)}.
\]

title: The mirror's composition across its temperature range
text:
Decimal. Supplementary scripts: the mirror's (folder \file{MIR}, checks D1, D2 and E0 to E7) and the cosmology check's (folder \file{CHECK\_COS}). T14 carries $\xi$ from the gravitational floor to the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448$), with a hot-deposit estimate near $4 \times 10^{-3}$. At the top of the ceiling range the floor was $2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ with the production coefficients first imported, and the computation below was first made there; with the derived coefficients and the mean energy per creation event it is $6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(iii)), and the two scripts were run again on 18 November 2026 with that value added to their grids.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] At $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, the floor when this was computed and now the floor for a reheating below the top of the ceiling range (the floor goes as $T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3/4}$), the mirror is charge-dominated and degenerate from the moment it is seeded: the Fermi energy its deposited baryon number must carry exceeds the thermal deposit there by $49$ to $84$, and at its weak freeze-out the quark chemical potential is $18$ to $23$ times its temperature. Beta equilibrium persists into the hadron phase, and for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$ (our tower's sphaleron value $L/B = -51/28$, or zero) the mirror ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons. At $\xi = 6.6 \times 10^{-4}$, the present floor at the top of the ceiling range, the same scripts give a mirror that is still neutron-rich for $L \leq 0$ but only moderately degenerate: the Fermi energy exceeds the thermal deposit by $2.7$, the quark chemical potential is $3.5$ times the temperature at seeding and $3.7$ times at $T' \approx 0.4$ GeV (the quantity that is $18$ to $23$ at the lower values), beta equilibrium still lasts into the hadron phase, and the mirror ends $96$ percent neutrons for $L/B = -51/28$ and $83$ percent for $L = 0$. So ``charge-dominated and degenerate from the moment it is seeded'' holds at $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ and holds at the present floor only in this weaker form: the charge still dominates, by a factor near three and not by fifty or more. At either value the endpoint is cold, dense, neutron-rich matter; the composition after decay and capture needs a dense-matter network and is not computed here.
\item[(ii)] Between $\xi \approx 3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing T14's hot-deposit estimate, the mirror is helium ($Y' = 0.94$ to $1.00$).
\item[(iii)] Above that interval the helium fraction falls ($Y' = 0.85$ at $\xi = 0.1$) and towards the cap the mirror is hydrogen-rich ($Y' = 0.58$ at $\xi = 0.448$).
\end{enumerate}
T14 does not print a mirror $\eta'$ at freeze-out; its floor value ($19$ to $26$ as printed, $2.1$ with the derived coefficients and the mean energy per creation event) is the late-time ratio, and the thermal up-down ratio T14 assumes there is inconsistent with its own $\eta' > 1$.
proof: Computed, as the source states, in the supplementary scripts \file{MIR} (checks D1, D2 and E0 to E7) and \file{CHECK\_COS}, across the range of the temperature ratio that \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} and \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} supply, for the mirror that \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one} makes a copy of this tower. The source gives no further proof text. Clause (i) was first computed at $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, the floor of \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} at the production coefficients first imported; the floor there is now $6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ (derived coefficients, mean energy per creation event). The statement at the present floor is from a second run of the same two scripts on 18 November 2026, each changed in one line, the grid of $\xi$, to which $5.2 \times 10^{-4}$, $6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ and $8.1 \times 10^{-4}$ were added; the mirror's script passes its $24$ checks as before and reproduces the figures at $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$. At $\xi = 6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ the cosmology check gives the ratio of Fermi energy to thermal deposit as $2.7$ ($84$ and $49$ at $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$) and the quark chemical potential over the temperature as $3.5$ at seeding and $3.7$ at $T' \approx 0.4$ GeV ($23.4$ and $17.8$ there). The mirror's script, with its degeneracy-aware weak freeze-out in the hadron phase, gives freeze-out at $T' = 18$ MeV with $n/p = 22$ and neutron fraction $0.957$ for $L/B = -51/28$, and at $T' = 111$ MeV with $n/p = 5.0$ and neutron fraction $0.832$ for $L = 0$ (at $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$: $1.000$, $0.999$ and $0.965$, $0.954$); for a positive lepton number $L_{e}/B = 0.875$, outside the clause, it gives $0.32$. Its thermal-rate table, the paper's own method, puts the late-time ratio $\eta'$ at $2.12$ and the quark chemical potential at freeze-out at $1.8$ times the temperature, where it has $10$ and $8.6$ at the lower values. On the helium branch, which is not the branch the mirror takes there for $L \leq 0$, the same run puts the deuterium bottleneck at $T' = 0.185$ MeV with $\eta' = 2.13$ and a baryon density of $4.3 \times 10^{29}$ per cm$^{3}$, and the burning reheats the mirror's plasma by $1.86$ ($3.23$ and $2.96$, with $1.3 \times 10^{31}$ and $7.6 \times 10^{30}$ per cm$^{3}$, at $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$). For comparison the run gives, at $\xi = 5.2 \times 10^{-4}$, the ratio $7.1$, neutron fractions $0.984$ and $0.887$ and a reheat of $2.16$, and at $8.1 \times 10^{-4}$, the ratio $1.2$, neutron fractions $0.916$ and $0.771$ and a reheat of $1.64$; the ratio of Fermi energy to thermal deposit passes one at $8.5 \times 10^{-4}$, the crossover of the cited Proposition. These are decimal results of scripts that are not in the store: no check of them is added, and the composition after decay and capture is not computed at any of these values.

title: The mirror against the astrophysical record
text: On every branch the mirror recombines early (at a visible temperature of $0.04$ to $3$ keV) and is cold dark matter for the microwave background and large-scale structure, and in galaxies it is a collisional gas that cools by bremsstrahlung in a few gigayears, settles partly and forms stars. Against the Gaia thin-disk bounds \cite{Widmark2021} and Roux and Cline's limit $\Omega_{b'} \lesssim 0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ \cite{RouxCline2020}, only the helium interval has room: there T14b's Galaxy models pass at the Sun only with helium-star feedback \cite[Obs.~9.1]{ButlerT14b}, and Roux and Cline's limit, which covers the whole helium interval, is exceeded by a factor $1.24$. Nothing in the construction lowers the mirror's share below $0.995$ or changes its microphysics without a further exception to P2: the copy is exact and the tension T14 records stands. (The cold mirror itself is an exception to P2 at its version-1 reach; P2 as scoped leaves $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needs a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}.) Observation level, on imported galaxy modelling.

title: From content to matter
text: This section uses imported physics (gauge theory in three and five dimensions, \claimref{rule2.imported-parity-anomaly} and \claimref{rule2.imported-five-dimensional-chern-simons-shift}, and the published dark-plasma bounds) and decimal estimates, labelled; every number is reproduced by Part K of the script or by the named supplementary check. Its decimal estimates take T14's particle model (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule}): the quanta's mass is the nucleon's and $d$ is this world's baryon spacing, $d_{b} \approx 0.98$ m. E alone fixes the mass density and leaves both the number of quanta and $d$ free, so a statement below that uses a number density or the value of $d$ is conditional on that model. The five-dimensional statements of Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-towers}(i), (ii) and (iv) need only $LT \gg 1$; the radiation caps of (iii) scale with $LT$.

title: The phases of the three-dimensional towers
proof: Follows from \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i) (the minimal bare level), \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-content} (the cells and their charges) and, for $r = 7$, \claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit}, together with the imported results the source names (Polyakov confinement; the topological mass and the absence of confinement at nonzero level, after Deser, Jackiw and Templeton and Affleck, Harvey, Palla and Semenoff; flux attachment, after Wilczek), as the source states. Those imported results are not in the store.

title: Survival of sheet relics against annihilation
text: Decimal. On a sheet the comoving number per unit area and the expansion rate both fall as $a^{-2}$ in radiation domination, so two-dimensional s-wave annihilation with $\sigma_{1}v = 2P/m$ ($P$ the absorption probability per encounter) depletes a symmetric population logarithmically, $1/N_{f} = 1/N_{0} + (2P/m)\ln(a_{f}/a_{i})/(a^{2}H)$. At the particle model's density a symmetric sheet relic keeps $99$ percent of its number only for $P$ below $1$ to $2 \times 10^{-16}$, the range spanning the number of relativistic species; at $P = 1$ a fraction of order $10^{-14}$ survives ($1.2 \times 10^{-14}$ with the inputs here, K3; T14 gives about $3 \times 10^{-14}$ for the same estimate \cite[Sec.~7.7]{ButlerT14}). In phase (T) this needs $e^{2}/m$ above $7 \times 10^{7}$ to $9 \times 10^{7}$, which also makes the relic collisionless in clusters (threshold $5.9 \times 10^{6}$, from the in-sheet phase-shift bound $1.7 \times 10^{-7}$ of T14b's cluster computation \cite[Comp.~3.3, Prem.~2.12]{ButlerT14b}) (K4). Phase (C) fails the particle model's density by itself.
proof: Follows from the density of \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-unit-ball-rule}, with the particle model's count, R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) and R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}), for the number of quanta, the phases (T) and (C) of \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases} and the in-sheet phase-shift bound of \claimref{simulations.cluster-bound-two-dimensions}, as the source states; the decimal estimates are those the source cites to its script (K3, K4).

title: The five-dimensional towers in cosmology and halos
text:
Decimal, with imports as stated. With the fifth direction one $d$ deep and co-expanding (R3), and $d = d_{b}$ (the particle model, R1 and R2; \cite[Prem.~7.4, Rem.~7.9, Rem.~7.14]{ButlerT14}). Under E alone the depth has no stated value, and the numbers below are conditional on the particle model's:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $LT$ runs from about $390$ (at $g_{s} = 106.75$) to $1170$ today: the Kaluza-Klein spacing is always below $T/120$, so the towers are five-dimensional at the visible temperature and at their matter's mass scale (K5); at T14's small dark temperatures the dark bath itself is only a few Kaluza-Klein levels deep.
\item[(ii)] Five-dimensional gauge theory is infrared free; reducing to four dimensions gives a confinement scale below $\pi/L$ by a factor smaller than $e^{-250}$ even at strong coupling (K7), and the $1/r^{2}$ potential binds nothing unless the theory is within a factor of about eight of strong coupling at the quark mass (supplementary \file{D5C}, H3; \cite{CLP2000}). There are no dark hadrons and no dark atoms.
\item[(iii)] With the Kaluza-Klein tower populated, $\Delta\Neff < 0.3$ needs $T_{D}/T_{\gamma} < 0.085$ for the nine vectors of $\uu(3)$ ($0.13$ for one photon), not the $0.46$ to $0.51$ of T14's zero-mode formula \cite[Prop.~6.3]{ButlerT14}; a sector decoupled at a GeV would give about $670$ (K6). T14's own temperature estimates meet the corrected bound by orders.
\item[(iv)] Two-body scattering is collisionless by geometry, $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}/m = \sigma_{5}/(Lm) < 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$ even for charged and coloured species (supplementary \file{D5C}, H9).
\item[(v)] With no boundary term in the series the gauge field's natural condition at the ends of the fifth direction keeps a four-dimensional zero mode, so beyond about a metre the charged species form a neutral dark plasma. Published plasma-instability limits \cite{SSS2024, PIC2024}, rescaled to a GeV, lie six to ten orders below the coupling a freeze-out relic needs and about two to five orders below a deposit at a natural five-dimensional coupling (supplementary \file{D5C}, checks I3 and I4, and \file{CHECK\_COS}). Whether such instabilities transfer bulk momentum in a merger is not established \cite{Lasenby2020}: an exposure, not an exclusion.
\item[(vi)] If the neutral species $N$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.five-dimensional-content}) carries the particle model's count as a deposit and the charged species annihilate at weak coupling, the tower carries no long-range charge and is collisionless whatever the zero modes do. Under Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule} this branch is open to both five-dimensional towers.
\end{enumerate}
The relic is a symmetric gas of free spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ dark quarks and leptons, or of $N$ alone. The lightest species is stable by fermion parity, the lightest quark and lepton by species numbers broken only at the rung scale.

title: Neither E nor the particle model has a mechanism in the odd towers
text: In this tower and the mirror a quantum's mass is a confinement scale, $m = c\Lambda$ \cite[Prop.~4.7]{ButlerT14}. title: From content to matter
The kinematics of the sterile towers
proof:
\textit{(i) Sums of null vectors.}\enspace For non-null $v$, $v^{\perp}$ is three-dimensional, of signature $(1,2)$ if $Q(v) > 0$ and $(2,1)$ if $Q(v) < 0$, since the counts of \claimref{synthesis.completion-recovers-the-real-clifford-algebras}(iii) add over $V = \R v \perp v^{\perp}$. Either way $Q$ is indefinite on it, so it takes the value $-Q(v)/4$ at some $w \perp v$, and then
\[
Q\bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}v \pm w\bigr) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{4}Q(v) + Q(w) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{4}Q(v) - \tfrac{1}{4}Q(v) \;=\; 0
\]
(J1, which also checks nondegeneracy and indefiniteness on random vectors, and J2, which exhibits sums of both signs).



\emph{(i) The cone is connected.}  In coordinates $(t_{1}, t_{2}; x_{1}, x_{2})$ with $Q = t_{1}^{2} + t_{2}^{2} - x_{1}^{2} - x_{2}^{2}$, the null cone minus the origin is
\[
\bigl\{\, |t| = |x| > 0 \,\bigr\} \;\cong\; S^{1} \times S^{1} \times \R_{>0},
\]
which is connected. In signature $(1,3)$ the same set has the two components $t_{0} > 0$ and $t_{0} < 0$. T16 proves the corresponding statement for the timelike sets \cite[Lem.~4.4]{ButlerT16}.



\emph{(ii)}  $Q$ is a sum of four squares, so $Q(v) = 0$ only at $v = 0$ (J3).

title: The Kleinian algebra
text: At $r = 0$ the constituent field is $\R$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}), and $\Cl^{0}(2,2) \cong \Mat_{2}(\R) \oplus \Mat_{2}(\R)$ has two inequivalent spinor ideals. There is no time direction, so no adjoint and no norm clause: a momentum bilinear in one element of each ideal is preserved by acting with $U$ on the elements of the first ideal and $U^{-T}$ on those of the second, for every $U \in GL(n,\R)$ (supplementary \file{STE}, checks C4, C5). Under H2 with this slot group the gauge algebra is the split form $\sll(2,\R) \oplus \sll(3,\R) \oplus \gl(1,\R)$, of dimension $12$, whose simple factors have indefinite Killing forms, signatures $(2,1)$ and $(5,3)$ (E5): there is no positive gauge-kinetic energy. T14's ``Kleinian copy of the Standard Model'' \cite[Cor.~3.11]{ButlerT14} needs a compact weak factor, which does not preserve that bilinear. Assembly level.

title: Dark matter and the dark towers
Introduction
text:
The dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} derives eight parallel towers, one per residue $r = p - q \bmod 8$ of the real Clifford algebras, and finds that six can hold matter: this one ($r = 6$, signature $(1,3)$), its mirror ($r = 2$, $(3,1)$), two three-dimensional towers ($r = 1, 7$) and two five-dimensional towers ($r = 3, 5$). The towers touch only through the one shared metric. By its unit-ball rule the five dark towers hold, relative to our baryons, the shares $1$, $4/3$, $4/3$, $8/(3\pi)$ and $8/(3\pi)$, whose sum $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$ is the observed ratio of dark to visible matter. T14 proves the mirror a copy of this tower; for the four odd towers it says how much matter each holds and leaves open what that matter is.

This note answers that question by doing in each tower what the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} does in ours. T12's chain is: a constituent; the number of constituents at which mass begins; the mixings that preserve total momentum; the automorphisms of the smallest massive composite, identified with the gauge algebra; the content and its charges; then, with imported physics, hadrons, atoms and a stable relic. Every link is transposed here, and where the transposition meets an obstacle the resolution is taken from the way our tower resolves the same obstacle.

Everything is written in geometric algebra. A constituent is an element of a minimal left ideal of an even Clifford algebra; its momentum is the vector part of $\psi e_{t} \rev{\psi}$; its field of scalars is the corner algebra $f \Cl^{0} f$ with the adjoint $x^{\dagger} = e_{t}\rev{x}e_{t}^{-1}$. The mass laws are identities of the reversion pairing $\rev{\psi}_{1}\psi_{2}$.

title: Prior art
text: The real Clifford algebras, their periodicity and their spinor modules are classical (Cartan, Chevalley \cite{Chevalley1954}, Lounesto \cite{Lounesto2001}); the even-subalgebra isomorphisms $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl(p,q-1)$ and $\Cl^{0}(p,q) \cong \Cl^{0}(q,p)$ are standard \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001}, and the division algebra of each even algebra can be read off the periodicity table. The spacetime-algebra current $j = \psi\gamma_{0}\rev{\psi}$ and its square $j^{2} = |\psi\rev{\psi}|^{2}$ are Hestenes's \cite{Hestenes1966, DoranLasenby2003}. Mirror matter and its cosmology have a long literature \cite{FootMirror2004, RouxCline2020}; the parity anomaly and topologically massive gauge fields in $2+1$ dimensions are Redlich's and Deser, Jackiw and Templeton's \cite{Redlich1984, DJT1982}; Polyakov confinement \cite{Polyakov1977}; five-dimensional gauge theory, its Chern-Simons terms and its strong-coupling scale are standard \cite{IMS1997, CLP2000}. The identification of a gauge algebra with the automorphisms of the minimal massive composite is T12's, and its global form and content are classical structure theory once that identification is made.
