title: Results cited, not shown
The flag bit exists exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$
text: Let a tower have dimension $n$ and conformal completion with ambient $V$ of dimension $n + 2$, and let $W, W' \subset V_{\C}$ be a Witt pair, the two halves of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag} taken coherently across the pairs, with pure spinors the null blade $f$ and the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). Then the choice between $W$ and $W'$ is a discrete invariant of the connected conformal spin group, a \emph{bit}, if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (ambient dimension $2m$ with $m$ odd), and the bit is the chirality of the pure spinor, that is, the parity of the Fock grade of the complementary half's pure spinor ($0$ for $f$, $m$ for the top state). (i) The odd residues are odd-dimensional for every signature in the class, so the ambient is odd-dimensional, the pseudoscalar central, an even versor carries $W$ to $W'$, and the spin algebra mixes the Fock grades: no bit, on any window. (ii) The even residues carry the bit exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$: under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} all four are at dimension four and carry it; the causal representatives of the alternative windows of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii), $(1,1)$ of $r = 0$ and $(1,5)$ of $r = 4$, do not. So the towers that can be oriented are the even residues $\{0, 2, 4, 6\}$ given P3, and the odd residues cannot be, given nothing.

title: The mirror share is one, and how fragile that is
text:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), with the common ceiling and coupling of Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}, $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror as an equality of the charge $B - L$, and under Hypothesis (equal conversion) stated below; the equality of $\Lambda$ and $c$ is an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, the gravitational floor's value with the production coefficients first imported, the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, and at the present floor, $6.6 \times 10^{-4}$, it is moderately degenerate and ends $83$ to $96$ percent neutrons, in both cases a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So the mass factor of $f_{2}$ is exactly one, protected by the common-ceiling-coupling premise (Premise \claimref{synthesis.common-ceiling-coupling-premise}), and fragile; $f_{2} = 1$ itself holds under Hypothesis (equal conversion) in addition.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Hypothesis (equal conversion).} The mirror's ratio of baryon number to $B - L$ equals this tower's. It is not shown, and it is a stated hypothesis of this result, not a registered premise: the inherited charge is the total $B - L$, and the copy equates the two towers' $B - L$, not their baryon number (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i), version 11). The mirror's unit of the observed dark-to-baryon total $5.364$ is conditional on it.

title: Seeding by gravity: the floor on a dark tower's temperature
text:
By exact superselection the towers interact only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), so after the descent a dark tower can be heated only gravitationally; what the descent itself deposited in it (its charge, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, with whatever energy the deposit carried) is a datum, not a computation. Let the descent reheat this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and let tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, be heated by gravitational pair production from the visible plasma at the rate per volume $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gravitational-pair-production-from-the-operator-source-at-first-order}(v) (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate} for the published values), under that theorem's hypothesis (OS), or on the standard account of the Fact, with $c$ the sum of the theorem's per-species coefficients over the tower's light content and $\Gamma$ counting creation events, each of two quanta. Then the produced comoving yield of events is
\[
Y \;=\; \frac{c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}}{3\,\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}}, \qquad \kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s} \;=\; 145.3 \ \text{at } g_{*} = g_{s} = 100,
\]
and the number of quanta per unit entropy is $2Y$.

\emph{(The mean energy per event.)} A creation event puts into the tower the energy $E_{1} + E_{2}$ of the incoming pair. In the rate integral of clause (v) of that theorem the angular weight of every channel is a constant times $s^{2} = 4E_{1}^{2}E_{2}^{2}(1 - \cos\theta_{12})^{2}$, so each incoming leg is weighted by $E^{3}$ times its occupation, independently of the other leg, and the mean energy of a leg is
\[
\frac{\Gamma(5)\,\zeta(5)}{\Gamma(4)\,\zeta(4)}\,T \;=\; \frac{4\,\zeta(5)}{\zeta(4)}\,T \;\approx\; 3.832\,T \ \ \text{(Bose)}, \qquad
\frac{\tfrac{15}{16}\cdot 24\,\zeta(5)}{\tfrac{7}{8}\cdot 6\,\zeta(4)}\,T \;=\; \frac{30\,\zeta(5)}{7\,\zeta(4)}\,T \;\approx\; 4.106\,T \ \ \text{(Fermi)},
\]
with $\zeta(4) = \pi^{4}/90$ and $1.0369277 < \zeta(5) < 1.0369278$. An event from a Bose pair therefore carries $8\,\zeta(5)/\zeta(4)\,T \approx 7.664\,T$ on average and an event from a Fermi pair $(60/7)\,\zeta(5)/\zeta(4)\,T \approx 8.212\,T$. For a produced species $j$ the mean energy per event $\bar{E}$ weights these two by the Bose and Fermi parts of $\alpha_{j}$ in clause (v), which are proportional to $\bigl(c_{j}(N_{s} + 12N_{v}) + 5\tau_{j}\sum_{i}\tau_{i}\bigr)/225$ and to $49\,c_{j}N_{w}/4800$; for a tower the parts are summed over its light content. So $7.66 < \bar{E}/T < 8.22$ for every bath and every content, and for a bath of the Standard Model's content $(N_{s}, N_{w}, N_{v}) = (4, 45, 12)$ with zero curvature couplings
\[
\bar{E} \;=\; 7.873\,T \ \text{(a real scalar)}, \qquad 7.890\,T \ \text{(a chiral fermion, or a real massless vector, or any number of them)}, \qquad 7.889\,T \ \text{(a copy of that content)}.
\]

\emph{(The floor.)} With $s/\rho = 4/(3T)$ at $g_{*} = g_{s}$ the energy fraction at production is $\tfrac43(\bar{E}/T)\,Y$, between $10.49\,Y$ and $10.52\,Y$ for those contents, and the temperature ratio it alone would give is
\[
\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \;=\; \Big(\tfrac43\,\frac{\bar{E}}{T}\,Y\,\frac{g_{*}}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4} \;=\; 1.23 \times 10^{-3}\; c^{1/4}\Big(\frac{16}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4}\Big(\frac{T_{\mathrm{desc}}}{6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV}}\Big)^{3/4}
\]
for $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ at the reheating. The prefactor depends on the produced content only through $\bar{E}^{1/4}$: it lies between $1.225$ and $1.226 \times 10^{-3}$ for each of the contents above, and between $1.21$ and $1.24 \times 10^{-3}$ for any bath and content. This is a floor: the tower's bath cannot be colder, and it is hotter by whatever energy the deposit carried. The ratio thereafter evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, by
\[
\left(\frac{g_{d}^{\mathrm{seed}}}{g_{d}}\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{g_{s}}{g_{s}^{\mathrm{seed}}}\right)^{1/3}
\]
at any later epoch. Two inputs are not fixed by the formula: $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the ceiling of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} or below it, so that across that range the floor spans a factor $(3.5 \times 10^{11}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3/4}$, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ ($3.75 \times 10^{-3}$), the body quoting the top and saying so; and the deposit's energy, which sets the actual ratio above the floor.

title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number
text:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes a count of registered units, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the light rays number $2\pi N^{2}/(c\ln 2)$ for $c$ boundary-mode arrays per light ray (\claimref{synthesis.the-residue-requires-two-arrays-per-unit-on-average-and-fixes-no-grouping}(iii)), and $c$ depends on the tower's content, a five-dimensional field counting one array set per Kaluza-Klein level, equivalently one per resolution cell of the extra direction, so the common count is that of registered units, not of light rays or of boundary modes; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. Three objects have carried the word charge in the stored statements, and they are kept apart here: the residue label $r$ of the tower, constant on the tower's sector, which is what the superselection rule is about (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}, step 1); the total $B - L$ of the tower's matter; and its baryon number $n_{B}$, which is what the measured baryon density reads. By the maintainer's decision of 12 November 2026, $Q$ is the second, the total $B - L$ (Premise \claimref{synthesis.matter-asymmetry-registered-free-input}); the naming is a decision and not a result of this Proposition. What then holds at any mirror temperature is that the mirror carries the same $B - L$ as this tower. The mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ is an equality of baryon number, and it follows from the equal $B - L$ only if the mirror's ratio of baryon number to $B - L$ equals this tower's. That is not shown: in this tower the ratio is the equilibrium coefficient of the anomalous weak process, if that process equilibrated after the descent (a coefficient that is not a stored Fact, $\tfrac{28}{79}$ for one light doublet and $\tfrac{8}{23}$ for two, \claimref{synthesis.abelian-charges-of-the-sixteen-and-the-terms-that-break-them}(vi)), a number for a hot plasma, and at $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$, the floor's value with the production coefficients first imported, the mirror's plasma is degenerate from the moment it is seeded, and at the present floor of (iii) it is still degenerate there, though moderately: its quark chemical potential is $3.5$ times its temperature at seeding, where it is $18$ to $23$ at the lower values (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). So $f_{2} = 1$ at any mirror temperature is conditional on that equality of ratios; given it, a cold mirror carries the same baryon number as this tower, with negligible mirror radiation. The words ``equal baryon number'' in (iii) and the comparison of (iv) are read under the same condition.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The three objects of (i) have three different statements. \emph{Between towers.} The residue $r$ is superselected, and the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), yields $3.9 \times 10^{-14}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating ($1.95 \times 10^{-14}$ creation events of two quanta each, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(iii)) against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than three orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. So the mirror's matter is not supplied from this tower after the descent. Superselection of $r$ forbids exchange between towers and implies nothing about a charge within a tower. \emph{Within a tower, $B - L$.} For one family, of the terms the store holds only the Majorana element changes $B - L$: the electroweak mass terms conserve it, the $24$ slot-pair generators carry it, and its mixed weak coefficient vanishes (\claimref{synthesis.abelian-charges-of-the-sixteen-and-the-terms-that-break-them}(ii) to (v)). Premise \claimref{neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy} states that the descent reheats below the lower heavy scale, so that no heavy state thermalised and the descent's $B - L$ is untouched. So, argued and not proved, the charge $Q$ is the descent's and is not produced afterwards given that Premise, with the Majorana element the named exception: no rate of that element is computed with or without the Premise, the non-thermal injection by descent-populated heavy states vanishes only under the real-breaking assumption (\claimref{neutrino.leptogenesis-suppressed-alignment-reheating-premise-new}), and nothing is shown beyond one family. \emph{Within a tower, baryon number.} That it cannot be produced afterwards is not asserted. The $24$ slot-pair generators do not commute with $n_{B}$ (\claimref{synthesis.baryon-number-centraliser-in-the-five-mode-algebra}(iii); \claimref{synthesis.abelian-charges-of-the-sixteen-and-the-terms-that-break-them}(iv)), and no bound on their rate is stored; and the anomalous weak process, on the imported statement that it changes a charge of non-zero mixed weak coefficient (not a stored Fact), changes $n_{B}$ and keeps $B - L$, and its equilibrium, which the check of Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition} uses, produces baryon number from $B - L$ after the descent. The $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy are then a figure derived from the datum, conditionally, as the Premise on $\epsilon$ states. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes; that is an exception at P2's version-1 reach, P2 as scoped leaving $\xi$ free, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}, and the cold mirror then needing a non-equilibrium descent, Proposition \claimref{synthesis.cold-mirror-needs-non-equilibrium-descent}), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi = 6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), with the derived production coefficients, which close the earlier species-counting bracket, and the mean energy per creation event computed from the rate; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $2.1$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere between the floor and the hot deposit; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the cold end: at $\xi = 2.8$ to $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ (the floor's value with the coefficients first imported) the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, and at the present floor $6.6 \times 10^{-4}$ it is moderately degenerate and ends $83$ to $96$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate and not the floor (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). The burning branch is therefore not the floor's composition.

title: Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

title: Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).

title: The two families are the two chiralities
Type by residue, and what each tower can carry intrinsically
The unit-ball rule
text:
Under Premises E (\claimref{dark-matter.e-equal-mass-per-unit-ball}) and R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}), with the four odd towers populated (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}) and residues $0$ and $4$ empty (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four}):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The rule.)} The share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $f = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; V_{3}\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{V_{D_{r}}}
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{3}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}
\;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.36432\ldots
\]
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The quanta do not enter.)} Only the mass per unit ball enters. A filling that keeps E has the shares of (i) whatever its quanta weigh and however many they are. Premises R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) and R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}), in R2's common length, imply E in that length, so the rule holds under R1 to R3, as it was first stated; they are not needed.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(E and R3 are the closed form's shares, tower by tower.)} Write $\rho_{r}$ for the mass density of the tower of residue $r$ in its own space, $r = 6$ this world, let the three-dimensional towers' sheets be $s$ apart and let the five-dimensional towers' matter count through a length $t$ of the extra direction, so that in the sourcing rule
\[
f_{r} \;=\; \frac{\rho_{r}}{s\,\rho_{6}} \;\; (r = 1, 7), \qquad f_{2} \;=\; \frac{\rho_{2}}{\rho_{6}}, \qquad f_{r} \;=\; \frac{\rho_{r}\,t}{\rho_{6}} \;\; (r = 3, 5) .
\]
Then there is a length $d$ for which E holds with $s = t = d$, as R3 requires, if and only if $s = t$, each three-dimensional tower's share is $\tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}$, each five-dimensional tower's share is $\tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}$ and the mirror's share is $1$. In particular, for any densities of a three-dimensional tower and of this world the length $d = \rho_{1}V_{2}/(\rho_{6}V_{3})$ is the only one at which the two hold equal mass per ball, and with the sheets that far apart that tower's share is $\tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}$ whatever the two densities are: there E with R3 puts no condition on the densities, it defines $d$ from them. The conditions that remain are that the other three-dimensional tower has the same density, that the mirror has ours, and that each five-dimensional tower has $\rho_{r}V_{4}d = \rho_{6}V_{3}$, which is its share. So E with R3 says what the closed form's shares say, tower by tower, and that the two thicknesses are one length, an equality the total does not see. The total says less than either: it fixes only the sum of the shares.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(One length.)} With towers of more than one space dimension populated, as Premise \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated} has it, E cannot hold in two different lengths: equal mass per ball at $d$ and at $d' \neq d$ would make $(d'/d)^{D}$ take one value at $D = 2$, $3$ and $4$.
\end{enumerate}
The agreement of (i) with the observed value is built in, not predicted: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, and its clauses were chosen with it known, and the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates within the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}). By (iii) the premises say what the closed form's shares say, with the two thicknesses equal, so they give the fit no support that is independent of the fitted number.

\emph{What the total rests on.} On the stored dependence edges the past cone of this closed form holds these postulates of the dark-matter subject: E and R3; P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), through the sourcing rule in which the shares are read (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}); P2 and P3, through the census of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}; and the two conditions registered as premises on 10 November 2026, the single-ideal clause \claimref{dark-matter.single-ideal-at-residues-zero-and-four} and the population of the odd towers \claimref{dark-matter.odd-towers-populated}. Until 19 November 2026 the cone held R1 and R2 in place of E, with R3's unit each tower's own cell radius and R2 entering twice; one length now does both jobs, as the radius of E's ball and as R3's unit. The democracy premise (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}) is not among them: it is E at the de Sitter radius, given the stored reading of the sphere form (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.dark-to-baryon-total-uses-r1-r2-and-d-only-as-mass-per-unit-ball}(ii)), a reading of its own. The total remains a fit. The mirror's share of one is derived separately (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}), so the closed form fixes two shares, $\tfrac{4}{3}$ and $\tfrac{8}{3\pi}$, against one measured number, the remainder $4.36 \pm 0.07$. Chosen with that number known, by the store's own record: the relation was found by solving for the observed value (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(i)); the clauses of the contact mechanism that returns R3's value were chosen with it known (the same, (ii)); the single-ideal clause was chosen knowing that the fit needs it (the same, (vi)); and the population of the odd towers is inferred from the remainder itself (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). P1, P2 and P3 belong to the paper's earlier sections, written before the rule was proposed (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.setting-dark-matter-ratio-unit-ball}).

title: Imported: the five-dimensional Chern-Simons shift
text: A five-dimensional Dirac fermion of mass $m$ charged under a gauge field, integrated out, shifts the coefficient of the five-dimensional Chern-Simons term by $\tfrac12\sgn(m)$ (times the representation's cubic index for a non-abelian field); the sign is odd under the reflection of one spatial direction, so that the parity-violating term is present for a single species and absent for a pair whose contributions cancel. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Witten1996, IMS1997}.

title: Imported: the parity anomaly
text: A single two-component Dirac fermion of mass $m$ in $2{+}1$ dimensions, coupled to a $U(1)$ gauge field, has an effective action containing a Chern-Simons term at level $\tfrac12\sgn(m)$ up to a sign that flips between the two inequivalent two-component representations; the term is odd under the reflection of one spatial axis, so a single species breaks parity, while two species, one in each representation with equal mass (equivalently the four-component fermion with its parity-invariant mass term), induce no net Chern-Simons term. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{NiemiSemenoff1983, Redlich1984, AGW1984}.

title: The gauge algebra of the minimal massive composite
The global form: the quotient determined
Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). The $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ anomaly coefficient of the two doublets, $3Y_{Q} + Y_{L}$ with the three the colour multiplicity, is then the identity $3 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac12 = 0$; it would equal $1$ if the empty conformal spinor were listed as the particle instead, so the anomaly confirms the orientation the listing fixed. Pair counting fixes $|Y_{L}/Y_{Q}| = 3$; the parity fixes the sign.
\item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives
\[
(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},
\]
that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. (The listing by the opposite handedness is the conjugate of this one, the same spectrum in the opposite convention.) Under (S) the grade-$k$ states of a single conformal spinor are the $(0, k)$ components, the states with no slot mode and $k$ pair modes occupied (their content $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and weight $-2k$ match, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight), so their parity is the total parity and this listing is the same listing as in (1).
\item (Consistency, and uniqueness given the content; under (S) for the doublets.) With the content of (1) and (2), all four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} hold. Conversely, for the field content $Q = (2,3)$, $L = (2,1)$, $u^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $d^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $e^{c} = (1,1)$, all listed in one handedness, together with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or no fourth singlet, and $Y_{Q} = 1/6$ as the normalisation, the four conditions determine $Y_{L}$, $Y(e^{c})$ and $\{Y(u^{c}), Y(d^{c})\}$ uniquely, and the solution is the spectrum of (1) and (2). Both hypotheses are necessary: with a fourth singlet of unconstrained hypercharge the conditions admit a one-parameter family, and if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$ rather than zero.
\end{enumerate}

title: Imported: the pair systems and the two chirality halves
text: Let $W$ be a maximal isotropic (three-dimensional) subspace of $V_{\C}$ with a dual isotropic complement. The complexified ascended algebra acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, and its two chirality halves are $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, each of dimension four. Every nonzero conformal spinor (twistor) $u \in \CS$ is a pure spinor: it is the Fock vacuum of the system of three fermionic ladder pairs built on its own annihilator space $W_{u}$, every state of the module is generated from $u$ by those pair operators, and $\CS$ (respectively $\CSm$) is what the even (respectively odd) products generate. Conformal spinors are states of the pair algebra, not its operators. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT9} for the Fock model and the chirality halves; \cite[Thm.~5.3]{ButlerT9} for the pure-spinor and Fock-vacuum statements; the tower paper \cite[Thms.~4.2, 4.3]{ButlerT3} for the iterated pair structure (one qubit per rung, Witt index as capacity) within which this sits.

title: The internal symmetry ladder
text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form''.)

title: The pair count in dimension $n$
text: Let the ambient space of the completion in spacetime dimension $n$ have signature $(2, n)$, so that $V_{\C}$ has dimension $n + 2$ and carries a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form. title: The three involutions on each grade
How the pseudoscalar commutes
Completion recovers the real Clifford algebras; Sylvester's law of inertia in GA
text:
Let $F$ be an ordered field. A quadratic space over $F$ is a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space $V$ with $Q(\lambda v) = \lambda^{2}Q(v)$ and polar form $B(u, v) = \tfrac12(Q(u + v) - Q(u) - Q(v))$ bilinear (as in \claimref{obj.std-algebra.quadratic-space}, with $F$ for $\R$); its Clifford algebra is defined by the universal property of \claimref{obj.std-algebra.clifford-algebra} over $F$, in which $uv + vu = 2B(u,v)$. $F$ is \emph{Euclidean} if every positive element is a square. $\Cl_{F}(p,q,r)$ is the Clifford algebra of $F^{n}$, $n = p + q + r$, with an orthogonal basis of $p$, $q$, $r$ vectors of squares $1$, $-1$, $0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Completeness gives square roots.)} If $F$ is complete (every nonempty subset bounded above has a least upper bound), then $F$ is Euclidean.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Orthogonal bases by rejection.)} Every quadratic space over $F$ has a basis $u_{1}, \dots, u_{n}$ of mutually anticommuting vectors, $u_{i}u_{j} = -u_{j}u_{i}$ for $i \ne j$, obtained by repeated rejection $x \mapsto x - B(x, u)\,u^{-1}$ from vectors $u$ with $Q(u) \ne 0$. If $F$ is Euclidean, the basis can be chosen with $Q(e_{i}) \in \{1, -1, 0\}$, by $e_{i} = u_{i}/\sqrt{|Q(u_{i})|}$ where $Q(u_{i}) \ne 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sylvester's law of inertia.)} For any ordered $F$, the numbers $p$, $q$, $r$ of vectors with $Q > 0$, $Q < 0$, $Q = 0$ in an anticommuting basis do not depend on the basis: $r = \dim \operatorname{rad} V$, and $p$ (respectively $q$) is the largest dimension of a subspace on which $Q$ is positive (negative) definite. If $F$ is Euclidean, two quadratic spaces are isometric if and only if they have the same $(p, q, r)$, and then $\Cl(V, Q) \cong \Cl_{F}(p,q,r)$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The completion recovers the store's algebra.)} Let $\Cl_{\Q}(p,q,r)$ be the $\Q$-span of the blades with the blade product of Proposition \claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute} (structure constants $0$, $\pm 1$). If $\R$ is a complete ordered field, as premise (F4) takes it, then $e_{S} \mapsto e_{S}$ extends to an isomorphism $\Cl_{\Q}(p,q,r) \otimes_{\Q} \R \cong \Cl(p,q,r)$, and for every real quadratic space $\Cl(V, Q) \cong \Cl_{\Q}(p,q,r) \otimes_{\Q} \R$ with $(p, q, r)$ its inertia; through $r$ added hyperbolic planes it embeds in the nondegenerate $\Cl_{\Q}(p{+}r,q{+}r) \otimes_{\Q} \R$, the radical generators going to null vectors $e'_{k} + f'_{k}$ (Theorem \claimref{conformal.minimal-nondegenerate-completion}). So every real Clifford algebra of the store is, up to isomorphism, a rational Clifford algebra of a $\pm 1$ form, or a subalgebra of one, extended by scalars.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Over $\Q$ square classes remain.)} Over $\Q$, (ii) holds without the normalisation and the invariance of $(p, q, r)$ in (iii) holds, but the isometry criterion fails: $Q(\lambda u) = \lambda^{2}Q(u)$ fixes $Q(u)$ only up to a nonzero rational square. The line with $e^{2} = 2$ is not isometric to the line with $e^{2} = \pm 1$; its Clifford algebra, with $x\bar{x} = a^{2} - 2b^{2}$ for $x = a + be$, has no zero divisors, while $\Cl_{\Q}(1,0)$ has $(1 + e_{1})(1 - e_{1}) = 0$. The plane with $e_{1}^{2} = 2$, $e_{2}^{2} = 3$ has $x\bar{x} = a^{2} - 2b^{2} - 3c^{2} + 6d^{2}$ for $x = a + be_{1} + ce_{2} + de_{1}e_{2}$, which has no nontrivial rational zero, so its Clifford algebra is a division ring, while $\Cl_{\Q}(2,0)$ has zero divisors. Over any Euclidean field they become $\Cl(1,0)$ and $\Cl(2,0)$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(What is used.)} Clauses (ii) to (iv) use of the coefficient field only that it is ordered and, for the normalisation, Euclidean. Completeness enters (iv) only through (i).
\end{enumerate}

title: The ladder pairs satisfy the CAR, as vectors
text:
In $T_k$, the adjoined null pairs satisfy, exactly and at the level of vectors,
\[
v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0, \qquad w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0, \qquad v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}\,,
\]
for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$: a system of $k$ fermionic modes, with no normal-ordering, no completion, and no representation chosen. Adding a rung adds one mode and touches none of the existing relations.
